canDo: Can connect present, past and future into a 2-minute personal statement.
review: Less new material; rework the 3 grammar points with the most errors.
input: 2 sets each of mixed listening and reading material, focusing on spotting tenses and timelines.
output: Write 110 words on “past – present – future”; speak for 2 minutes on the same topic.
checkpoint: A mixed grammar sample of ≥25 questions; find your top three types of error and redo them.
challenge: Today’s challenge: record a 2-minute personal statement: your life now (présent), an important past experience (passé composé + imparfait) and a future plan (futur); when you play it back, check that all three times are there and mark one sentence you could improve.

questions.why: She says clearly that she liked her colleagues; the problem was « je ne voyais jamais le résultat de ce que je faisais ». Working hours aren’t a reason she gives.
Ten months’ training, a workshop two years later; fifteen years is the time she spent at the insurance company. All three numbers are in the text — match each to the right event.
She says herself « Je ne gagnerai pas plus … le métier ne survivra pas si personne ne le transmet ». The open day is one Saturday a month.
The text explicitly rules out loans (« restés stables ») and says clearly that staff numbers haven’t risen since 2021.
On weekdays the seats are all taken before 10 — it’s full, not empty or closed.
Two measures: booking seats online and requesting new posts. Charging and closing don’t appear.
« Le résultat est contrasté » — the workshops are all let, but the north hall still has no project. The first buildings have been decontaminated.
« sa toiture coûterait à elle seule près de deux millions » — à elle seule limits the scope.
About a hundred people compared with the original 240, but « dans des activités plus variées ».
He thought going back to school would be the hardest part; it was actually money — three years of training on half his income.
His own words contrast « si la formation existe » with « comment ils vivront pendant qu'ils la suivent ».
« un peu moins », not the same or more; what he stresses is a sense of meaning.
He compares explicitly: « C'est ça qui a tout changé, plus que la qualité du pain, qui elle n'a pas bougé ». Taking on an apprentice is a result, not a cause.
dix-huit mois = a year and a half. Three years is how long he has had the business, and twelve kilometres is a distance, not a time.
« pas avant d'avoir remboursé le matériel » is the only condition; three hundred baguettes is the figure already reached.
« nous en avons demandé deux de plus … nous n'en avons obtenu qu'un seul » — ne … que restricts; it doesn’t negate.
The reason is that Julien goes part-time from January. The number of adults went down.
« Je ne trouvais pas de logement, je dormais chez un collègue ». The job was interesting; the team is what later improved things.
« on décide plus vite, on discute moins » — the difference compared with France.
She cooks at the weekend and freezes portions for the week. Cooking every evening was her old habit (imparfait).
« je n'ai pas envie d'apprendre à quarante ans » — he clearly doesn’t intend to learn.
« Ça revient beaucoup moins cher que de commander, et on mange mieux » — both reasons are in this one sentence.
